A Vale rule from the dictionary's avoid fields

Source: R/dict-tools.R
dict_vale.Rd

dict_vale() writes one Vale substitution rule that replaces each spelling an entry lists under avoid by the entry's canonical spelling: its term, or, for a string entry with no term, its value. It says what it will write before it writes.

Usage

dict_vale(dict = NULL, path = "styles/Weft/Terms.yml", level = "warning")

Arguments

dict

A dictionary, as read_dict() returns, or NULL to read dict.yml at the project root. A dictionary with problems raises its error and nothing is written.

path

The rule file, relative to the project root: <styles>/<Style>/<Rule>.yml.

level

The rule's level: "suggestion", "warning" or "error".

Value

The path written or removed, invisibly; character() when nothing was changed.

Details

The rule matches each spelling as written (ignorecase: false): list a case variant as a spelling of its own. Spellings are keys of a regular expression in Vale, so their metacharacters are escaped; longer spellings come first.

It replaces only a file it wrote (the first line says so) and stops with an error on any other, on a path outside the project, and on a symbolic link or a folder in place of the rule file or its folders. When the project's own dictionary (dict = NULL) has no avoid left, a file it wrote is removed; a dictionary given as dict never removes anything. It never writes .vale.ini: when that file does not list the style in BasedOnStyles, it says what the file needs.
